text:
inc-bot: Incident alert — elevated 502/504 errors detected across edge -> gateway path. Pager triggered for oncall. @oncall paging... :rotating_light:

maya: seeing a surge of 502s in nyc region, started ~10:15 UTC. Error-rate 6.2% across requests to /v1/generate

tony: I can confirm. Traces show KV cache misses spiking and immediate fallback to cold-kv path. Latency also increased for requests hitting dedicated-pool-3

jamie: Is this the prefix cache invalidation rollout from last night? I thought that completed.

maya: That rollout finished, but looks like a short-lived config push to routing service reverted a bitmap — routes started marking a bunch of prefixes as uncached

neha: grabbing logs from routing: `curl http://router-admin/flags | jq .` shows `prefix_cache_enabled: false` for a subset of clusters

oncall: I'm here — will coordinate. First priority: reduce customer-facing 5xx. Suggested mitigation: flip fallback policy to use warm-kv replicas and throttle fanout.

tony: quick mitigation I can do: pin routing to previous config in staging and promote to prod. Rolling back the last config commit now.

ops-bot: deploy started by tony on routing-config (commit abc123) -> rolling restart of 6/6 routers

maya: after ~30s saw error-rate drop to 1.1% but still some 504s from long tail

jamie: I can add a short-term rule at edge to extend gateway timeout from 3s -> 6s for model-serving routes to allow KV warmup

neha: patching edge timeout in-flight: `./infractl set route-timeout --route /v1/generate --timeout 6s` (applied)

sara: logs show a reduction in 504s, latency improved for most requests. Customer impact reduced. Marking severity as Sev2 -> monitoring.

maya: recording timeline and actions. Need hotfix PR to prevent config regressions and a canary gate to block prefix_cache toggles without KV sanity check

tony: hotfix branch created: `fix/prefix-cache-guard` with tests. Will open PR and cut patch now. Also adding API guard in router-admin to disallow toggles during high-traffic windows.

oncall: Good. Action items:
- tony: merge hotfix and deploy (hotfix-2026-03-15)
- jamie: commit edge timeout revert after KV warms (revert in 1h)
- neha: add additional alert that detects prefix_cache flips and pages with low severity
- maya: update runbook with step to check `router-admin` flags and fallback policy
- sara: notify CSMs about reduced impact for affected customers

ops-bot: PR merged by tony -> routing-config v2.14.5 deployed

maya: runbook updated (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefix-cache.md) — added troubleshooting snippet and exact commands used above

neha: alerts tuned: increased aggregation window from 1m -> 3m for 502 spikes on gateway to reduce noise; added alert on `prefix_cache_enabled` flips (severity: P3)

jamie: edge timeout reverted back to 3s after checking kv warm status

sara: sent update to CSMs + posted status update to status.redwood.ai — customers with requests >50rpm had transient errors, majority unaffected

oncall: closing squarely but leaving follow-ups:
- postmortem owner: maya
- add synthetic test hitting prefix-cache boundary in canary pipeline
- review config promotion approvals in router-admin

maya: acknowledged. I’ll file the postmortem and schedule a short retro tomorrow 09:30 PT

inc-bot: Incident cleared — transitioned to post-incident review. Tags: routing, prefix-cache, hotfix, runbook, alerts

sara: thanks team. great coordinated response :clap:
